message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles using a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Go to [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/), enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and a health‑impact summary. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Visit [aqicn.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/). | Live AQI, trend graph, and forecast for the next 24 h. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Search “LA air quality” or look for a dedicated “Air Quality” section. | Often include a quick snapshot and links to official data. |
| **Mobile apps** (AirVisual, Plume Labs, BreezoMeter) | Download the app, allow location access. | Real‑time AQI, alerts, and health recommendations. |

### Quick steps to check now

1. Open a browser and go to **airnow.gov**.  
2. In the search box, type “Los Angeles” or your specific ZIP code (e.g., 90001).  
3. Click the result for Los Angeles.  
4. The page will display the current AQI, the main pollutant, and a health‑impact level (Good, Moderate, Unhealthy, etc.).

If you’re planning outdoor activities, the EPA’s AirNow site also offers a 24‑hour forecast and a “Health Advisory” section that tells you whether it’s safe to exercise, especially if you have asthma or other respiratory concerns.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what the AQI categories mean!
